# Resolving the Edge/Linker Twist Degeneracy in PORMAKE — Final Research Report

> 이 보고서는 PORMAKE가 2-connection edge(링커)를 배치할 때 연결축에 대한 비틀림(twist) 자유도를 결정하지 못하고 임의의 값으로 남겨두는 문제의 정밀 진단, 두 가지 하드 제약(완화 후 대칭성 불일치 / 수치적 강건성), 선행 연구(geonho42 fork 및 외부 도구), 후보 설계안들의 적대적 검증, 그리고 권장 구현안을 담는다. 기술 내용·식별자는 영어로 유지한다. 모든 핵심 주장은 `file:line` 또는 URL로 인용되며, 다수의 사실은 이 저장소의 `.venv`에서 직접 재현·검증되었다.

---

## 1. Problem statement & why it matters

PORMAKE builds a MOF by placing **node** building blocks (≥3 connection points) and **edge/linker** building blocks (exactly 2 connection points) onto a topology net, then fusing dangling `X` connection markers into real bonds.

A node has ≥3 connection points, so aligning those points onto a topology slot determines a **full 3D orientation** (a unique rotation). An edge has only **2** connection points. Aligning two antipodal direction vectors fixes the **connection axis** but leaves the **rotation about that axis — the linker "twist" — completely under-determined**. PORMAKE never resolves this DOF, so the linker's body (aromatic ring plane, substituents) lands at an **essentially arbitrary roll angle** that depends only on the orientation the building block happened to have in its source `.xyz`, not on chemistry or on the surrounding framework.

The project README already names this defect (`README.md:21`):

> *"linkers would be inserted with random rotation around the axis formed by two connection points."*

**Why it matters.** The twist angle physically sets:
- the **dihedral** between the linker's conjugated plane and each node's connector plane (electronic/structural property of the real material),
- inter-linker and linker–node **steric clashes** (whether the generated structure is physically sensible at all),
- reproducibility and chemical correctness of every downstream simulation that consumes the CIF.

> Note on "random": current placement is in fact **deterministic** (the arbitrary roll is a fixed function of the stored frame), but it is **arbitrary and chemically meaningless**. The real defect is *under-determination*, not RNG.

---

## 2. Precise diagnosis of the current code

### 2.1 Edge placement path

The edge loop builds a **2-point** target `LocalStructure` from the two node-side connection-point atoms and calls `locate_with_permutation` — the *only* orientation step an edge ever receives (`src/pormake/builder.py:536-543`):

```python
target = LocalStructure(np.array([r1, r1 + d]), [i1, i2])
located_edge, rmsd = locator.locate_with_permutation(target, edge_bb, perm)
located_edge.set_centroid(centroid)
located_bbs[e] = located_edge
```

The permutation `perm` is just `[0,1]`/`[1,0]`, chosen by node-type ordering, decided pre-scaling and reused (`src/pormake/builder.py:367-374`). No twist control exists anywhere in this path.

### 2.2 The `n_slices = 1` Euler-grid collapse

`Locator.locate()` is a brute-force Euler-angle grid + Hungarian assignment + Kabsch fit, the project's robust "search + match + fit" philosophy. **For a 2-point target this grid is explicitly switched off** (`src/pormake/locator.py:148-162`):

```python
n_points = p_coord.shape[0]
if n_points == 2:
    n_slices = 1          # <-- grid collapses to a single identity trial
...
alpha = np.linspace(0, 360, n_slices)   # = [0.]
beta  = np.linspace(0, 180, n_slices)   # = [0.]
gamma = np.linspace(0, 360, n_slices)   # = [0.]
```

So even if `locate()` were used for edges, it could not search the twist. (Edges actually use `locate_with_permutation`, which skips the grid entirely.)

### 2.3 The 2-point Kabsch twist degeneracy

`find_best_orientation` fits a single rotation via scipy on exactly two antipodal vectors (`src/pormake/locator.py:86-88`):

```python
U, rmsd = scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation.align_vectors(p, q)
return U.as_matrix().T, np.sqrt(np.square(rmsd) / len(p))
```

`locate_with_permutation` then applies that one rotation about `bb.centroid` (the **X-centroid**, `src/pormake/building_block.py:181-183`) to **all** atoms (`src/pormake/locator.py:253-266`). With only 2 vectors this fixes the axis but the twist is free.

**Verified empirically in this repo (`.venv`, scipy 1.15.3):**
```
2-vector align_vectors → warnings: ['UserWarning'] | rss: 0.0
```
scipy fires *"Optimal rotation is not uniquely or poorly defined"* and returns `rss = 0.0` — any twist about the axis is an equally optimal fit. The connection-point RMSD objective is **exactly flat** in the twist DOF; no RMSD-based search can pick it. The warning is **never caught** anywhere in `src/` (only references are `locator.py:62` docstring and `locator.py:87`), so it is a free, currently-ignored signal that the twist is unconstrained.

### 2.4 No later stage resolves it

- **Nodes** are re-located after scaling by Kabsch against the relaxed `local_structure`, fixing a full frame (`src/pormake/builder.py:386-416`). **Edges** only get the 2-point realign + translate (`src/pormake/builder.py:511-543`).
- The **Scaler** minimizes a length+angle objective (node-centered dot products) over fractional positions and a free 3×3 cell with L-BFGS-B (`src/pormake/scaler.py:359-364`; bounds at `:352-355`). Its objective contains **no edge-twist term** — verified the optimizer variables are positions + cell only.

**Conclusion:** there is exactly one real, well-localized free scalar — the twist angle `phi` about the fixed connection axis — and nothing in the pipeline ever sets it.

### 2.5 A safety fact that constrains any fix

Verified for E1, E26, E32, E50, E8: **both `X` connection-point atoms lie exactly on the connection axis through the X-centroid** (`Xoffaxis = 0.0000` for all). Therefore a Rodrigues rotation `R(u, phi)` about that axis through the centroid leaves both `X` atoms fixed, so the bond-fusion logic — which indexes `located_bbs[j].connection_point_indices[perm]` (`src/pormake/builder.py:585-591`) and fuses X-neighbor→X-neighbor (`src/pormake/builder.py:656-658`) — is **provably unaffected** by the twist rotation. This is the single most important enabling fact for any clean fix.

## 3. The two hard constraints and what they imply

### Constraint 1 — Post-relaxation symmetry ≠ ideal-net symmetry (no brittle symmetry rules)

`Scaler.scale` runs an **unconstrained** L-BFGS-B over all fractional positions (bounds `[0,1]`) and a **fully free** 3×3 cell (bounds `[None,None]`), against a **length+angle-only** objective with no symmetry pin (`src/pormake/scaler.py:347-364`). Atoms leave special Wyckoff positions; the relaxed point group is generically **lower** than the `.cgd` space group. The topology never recomputes symmetry — it only stores the static spacegroup string (`src/pormake/topology.py:106-107`) and an ideal-net edge classification (negative tags / sorted node-type pairs, `topology.py:219-240`, `:1046-1054`).

**Implication:** any rule keyed off the *ideal* net (edge-transitivity, edge-center site symmetry, spglib database ops) can be **wrong** post-relaxation. Even chemically equivalent edges may require **different** twists after relaxation. This is exactly why the geonho42 fork's approach is brittle (Section 4).

### Constraint 2 — Numerical robustness (mirror the Locator's philosophy, not a rule)

The Locator's philosophy is **search + match + fit** (Euler grid → Hungarian → Kabsch → keep min-RMSD), escalating to finer grids and chiral retries (`src/pormake/builder.py:270-321`). The Scaler is L-BFGS-B over real geometry. Any acceptable fix must resolve the twist by **explicit objective minimization on actual coordinates**, not a hand-tuned rule or magic threshold.

### What both constraints jointly imply

The fix must:
1. read **only post-scaler, post-node-placement Cartesian geometry** (the relaxation-surviving invariants — node frames, placed atom coordinates, bond vectors), never the ideal net; and
2. choose `phi` by a **numerical optimization** (analytic seed + grid/local refine, 1-D analogue of `locate()`), per edge so that equivalent relaxed environments converge to equal twists *emergently* and broken-symmetry environments diverge *correctly*.

## 4. Prior art

### 4.1 The geonho42 fork ("PORMAKE v2") — rejected; what to salvage

Upstream README links it and frames it as the acknowledged prior art for this exact bug (`README.md:18-23`). The fork's edge-rotation fix is **symmetry/rule-based, keyed off the IDEAL net space group**:

- Loads `database/spacegroup.json`, maps `topology.spacegroup → spacegroup_number`, then calls `spglib.get_symmetry_from_database()` to generate reference positions ([fork builder.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/geonho42/PORMAKE/main/pormake/builder.py)).
- **Discrete brute-force angle sweep** about the connection axis (`R.from_rotvec(angle * axis)`), loops like `for i in range(0,91,30)` / `for j in range(0,180,10)` ([fork pormake_v2.py](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/geonho42/PORMAKE/main/example/script/pormake_v2/pormake_v2.py)).
- Scores each angle by distance of a "representative atom" (furthest from axis) to **symmetry-generated placeholder atoms** (`Ne`/`Ar`/`Kr` ASE-tag hacks).
- **M3GNet** (TensorFlow MLIP) only as a secondary tiebreaker across discrete angle sets, plus a final MLIP relaxation.
- Hardcoded magic thresholds (`0.3`, `1.0`); deep coupling of spglib logic into the core `Builder.build()` signature; heavy deps (`m3gnet`, `pymatgen`, `tensorflow`); shipped as an out-of-tree script; explicit limitation *"Mixing multiple edge types is not currently supported"* ([fork README](https://github.com/geonho42/PORMAKE/blob/main/example/script/pormake_v2/README.md)).

**Why rejected:** it violates **both** constraints — it scores angles against the ideal space group that the Scaler breaks (Constraint 1), and its "search" is a coarse discrete sweep with magic thresholds, not a genuine objective optimization (Constraint 2) — and it is unacceptable on engineering grounds.

**What to salvage:** (a) the **rotate-about-connection-axis** primitive (`R.from_rotvec(phi * axis)`); (b) the **furthest-from-axis atom as the twist handle / observable**; (c) the idea of an **outer scorer over candidate angles**. **Discard:** spglib/`spacegroup.json`, placeholder-atom tag hacks, magic thresholds, m3gnet/pymatgen-for-energy, the `build()`/`build_by_type` coupling, and the mixed-edge-type limitation.

### 4.2 External tools & math

- **The degeneracy is canonical, not a PORMAKE bug.** Placing a 2-connected block by aligning only its 2 connection points is the rank-deficient **Kabsch/Wahba** problem: 2 vectors fix the axis, rotation about it is undetermined ([Wahba's problem](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wahba%27s_problem), [Kabsch algorithm](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Kabsch_algorithm)).
- **ToBaCCo 3.0** orients blocks via SVD/Kabsch over permutations of connection points but **does not resolve** the 2-point twist either ([tobacco_3.0](https://github.com/tobacco-mofs/tobacco_3.0)).
- **AuToGraFS** aligns only dummy `X` atoms (Hungarian + Kabsch), inherits the same degeneracy, and exposes a **manual** `Fragment.rotate(theta, axis=dummy0-dummy1)` plus a downstream **UFF4MOF/GULP** force-field relaxation — i.e., the manual/rule fallback we want to replace ([DCoupry/autografs](https://github.com/DCoupry/autografs); [J. Phys. Chem. A 2014, doi:10.1021/jp507643v](https://doi.org/10.1021/jp507643v)).
- **MOFBuilder (npj Comput. Mater. 2026)** decomposes the linker into cores/fragments/connection-groups and **refines geometry with L-BFGS-B** against the scaled lattice — the strongest precedent that the right answer is a **post-placement numerical optimization**, paralleling PORMAKE's own Scaler ([npj Comput. Mater. s41524-026-02086-x](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41524-026-02086-x)).
- **scipy already ships the closed-form fix.** `Rotation.align_vectors(p, q, weights=[inf, w])` ("align-constrain") **exactly** aligns the primary pair (the connection axis) then solves the 1-DOF rotation about it to best-fit a secondary vector ([scipy docs](https://docs.scipy.org/doc/scipy/reference/generated/scipy.spatial.transform.Rotation.align_vectors.html); [PR #17542](https://github.com/scipy/scipy/pull/17542)). **Verified working on the pinned scipy 1.15.3 in this repo:** `align_vectors(p, q, weights=[inf, 1.0])` returns residual `~2.2e-16`.
- **Minimal/edge-transitive net theory** (O'Keeffe & Yaghi; [Chem. Rev. 2020, 9b00648](https://pubs.acs.org/doi/10.1021/acs.chemrev.9b00648); [Nat. Rev. Mater. 2021, s41578-021-00287-y](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41578-021-00287-y)) explains *why* ideal edge-transitivity need not survive relaxation — reinforcing Constraint 1.

## 5. Candidate approaches — comparison & adversarial verdicts

Three designs were proposed and adversarially stress-tested (skeptic + implementation reviewer, with empirical probes in `.venv`).

| # | Proposal | Twist DOF handling | Objective | Fails C1? | Fails C2? | Adversarial verdict | Strongest objection |
|---|----------|--------------------|-----------|-----------|-----------|---------------------|---------------------|
| **P1** | **Seed-and-Refine**: node-frame geometric seed + 1-D steric/coplanarity refine, in a new `Locator` method | 1 scalar `phi` about `u`; numeric C2 period; perm branches | steric clash + coplanarity tie-break, on placed geometry | **No** (reads only relaxed coords) | **Partly** | **needs-work** (both reviewers) | Seed (coplanar) and steric refine point at **orthogonal** angles on the canonical BDC case → final answer decided by an **untuned weight**. Steric is near-flat/maximal at the coplanar pose. Period detection misclassifies E1 (self-RMSD@180 = 0.60 Å). Some stale facts (carboxylate "two O" recipe doesn't exist; `natural_cutoffs` import fallback). |
| **P2** | **Pure-numerical per-edge**: grid + Brent over steric/strain on relaxed geometry | 1 scalar `phi`; numeric period; cylindrical skip | steric clash (primary) + transverse-lobe strain (secondary) | **Yes** (skeptic) | **Yes** (skeptic) | **flawed** (skeptic) / **needs-work** (impl) | **The "primary" steric term has ZERO gradient in `phi` for the canonical carboxylate-linker + metal-node case** (built a real `tbo` framework: min edge-to-node distance flat to 0.0000 Å across all angles; nearest node atoms are *on-axis*, so rotation about that axis can't move them; true clashes are inter-linker, non-local, beyond the 6 Å cutoff). Method silently collapses onto the imposed coplanarity rule. Frame/centroid bug in pseudocode (optimizes before `set_centroid`, scoring linker at origin vs world-coord nodes). E1-is-C2 claim false. |
| **P3** | **Symmetry-orbit warm-start + global reconcile**: orbit-coherent seed + ONE global L-BFGS-B over all twists with soft orbit spring | 1 scalar per edge; global JAX/L-BFGS; orbit coupling `lambda` | global steric + soft per-orbit circular-variance spring | **Yes** (skeptic) | **Yes** (skeptic) | **needs-work** (both) | The "orbit" = negative tag `topology.node_types[e]` is a **crystallographic-asymmetric-unit artifact, not a twist class**: in pcu/tbo/dia/nbo/fcu **all** edges share one tag (→ single global spring = the C1 brittleness it claims to avoid, gated only by hand-tuned `lambda`); in acs-h one chemical linker splits across 3–4 tags (→ refuses to couple identical edges). Over-built; reads as "geonho in disguise." Impl reviewer: **ship Stage A (per-edge analytic) only, drop Stage B.** |

**Convergent findings across all three reviews (these are the load-bearing, verified facts):**

1. The **diagnosis is correct** in all three: `n_slices=1` collapse (`locator.py:148-150`) + 2-vector `align_vectors` degeneracy (`locator.py:87`), warning live in production.
2. The **architectural seam is clean and safe**: a new `Locator` method replacing the call at `builder.py:537-543`, applying `R(u, phi)` about the X-centroid. Bond fusion is **provably untouched** because both `X` atoms sit on the axis (verified `Xoffaxis = 0.0000`).
3. A **per-edge solve reading only relaxed coordinates satisfies C1 by construction.** No orbit/symmetry layer is needed or wanted (P3's orbit spring is the weakest, most-rejected idea).
4. **The objective is the hard part, and a pure local steric term is FLAT in `phi` for the canonical case** (P2's fatal finding, independently consistent with P1's measurement that steric peaks at the coplanar pose). Whatever objective is chosen **must be empirically proven non-flat in `phi` on a real HKUST-1/MOF-5 build before any optimizer is trusted.**
5. Several "established" facts were stale and are corrected here: `pyproject.toml` lists **`pymatgen>=2023.8.10`** (scipy is transitive only, not pinned — verified); `natural_cutoffs` is imported with an `ase.utils`→`ase.neighborlist` **fallback** (`building_block.py:16-19`); **E1 is NOT C2** about its axis (self-RMSD@180 = 0.60 Å, verified), so any "period = π" assumption is unsafe.

## 6. Recommended approach

> **Seed-from-relaxed-node-frames + 1-D numerical refine over a coplanarity-primary / steric-feasibility objective, per edge, as a new `Locator` method — shipped in two PRs (analytic core first, optional refine second).** This is essentially **P1 corrected by the adversarial findings**, with P2's frame bug fixed and P3's orbit layer dropped.

### 6.1 Rationale (why this, given the verdicts)

- **Constraint 1** is satisfied *by construction*: every input is post-scaler, post-node-placement Cartesian geometry already in scope in the edge loop — `r1/r2` from the re-fit relaxed node frames (`builder.py:527-531`), the two adjacent node blocks `located_bbs[i1]/[i2]` (`builder.py:522-523`), and the matched node-side atoms `a1,a2` (`builder.py:525`). Nothing reads `topology.spacegroup`, `edge_types`, or spglib. Per-edge independence means equivalent relaxed environments → equal twists *emergently*; broken-symmetry environments → distinct correct twists.
- **Constraint 2** is satisfied by genuine objective minimization (closed-form seed + 1-D grid + local refine), the exact 1-D analogue of `locate()`'s grid-then-keep-best (`locator.py:160-194`) and the builder's escalate-and-refine (`builder.py:286-321`).
- **The verdicts force two corrections to the naive version:**
  1. **Coplanarity/dihedral is the PRIMARY signal, steric is a hard feasibility filter — not the reverse.** The skeptic proved local steric is flat (or peaks at the wrong angle) for the canonical carboxylate-linker case. So the principled twist objective is **alignment of the linker's transverse plane to the relaxed node connector frames**, with steric used only to reject clashing minima.
  2. **No symmetry/orbit layer, no period assumption.** Always search the full `[0, 2π)` (cheap), or derive period from an **element-aware, Hungarian-matched** self-overlap with a *documented, sensitivity-tested* tolerance — never from the ideal net, and never assuming any specific linker is C2.

### 6.2 Reduced search space

After Kabsch fixes the axis `u = d/|d|` (`d` from `builder.py:531`), the only residual freedom is **one scalar `phi`** = rotation about `u` through the X-centroid (`bb.centroid`, `building_block.py:181`), applied to `edge_bb.atoms.positions` **before** `set_centroid` (or, to avoid the P2 frame bug, **after** `set_centroid` rotating world-space atoms about the world-space X-centroid — see 6.6).

- **Default:** search `phi ∈ [0, 2π)`.
- **Discrete branches (kept, not invented):** the existing perm `[0,1]/[1,0]` (`builder.py:367-374`) — leave intact. **Do not** add per-edge chirality enumeration (impl reviewer: scope creep, unnecessary for achiral linkers).
- **Degenerate guard (cylindrical/thin linker):** if the linker's max transverse radius < tol → twist genuinely free → freeze at deterministic seed, log it. **Correct the stale example linkers:** verified `transR` is **E50 = 1.35 Å, E8 = 2.46 Å, E1 = 2.36 Å, E26 = 1.57 Å, E32 = 4.99 Å** — these are NOT degenerate; the guard should fire only for truly cylindrical cases (a bare bond), so set the threshold well below ~1.3 Å.

### 6.3 Objective function (the corrected core)

For each edge, with `phi` applied as `R(u, phi)`:

```
minimize   E(phi) = D(phi)  +  w_clash * Clash(phi)
```

- **`D(phi)` — DIHEDRAL/COPLANARITY (primary, the signal that is actually non-flat).** For each end: build the linker's transverse plane near its `X`-neighbor (from `edge_bb.bonds`: e.g. E1 `X30→C3`, `X31→C15`, plus second-shell ring atoms; robustly via **PCA of the transverse atom distribution** to avoid the furthest-atom tie that affects ~23/219 linkers). Build the matching node connector frame from `a1`/`a2` and their bonded atoms (`bb1.bonds`, `bb2.bonds`) — read from relaxed coordinates. `D(phi)` = sum over the two ends of the squared sine of the dihedral mismatch (projected onto the plane ⊥ `u`). For a rigid linker one `phi` cannot satisfy both ends when relaxation made them non-coplanar → use a **least-squares compromise and REPORT the residual** (this is a genuine rigid-linker limitation; document it, do not hide it).
- **`Clash(phi)` — STERIC FEASIBILITY (filter, NOT primary).** Soft repulsion `Σ relu(s_ij − dist_ij)²` over (edge atom, neighbor atom within ~6 Å) using `natural_cutoffs` (import with the `building_block.py:16-19` fallback). **Critical exclusions (must-not-miss):** exclude the two intended fusion pairs (`a1,a2` and `connection_point_indices[perm]`) **and all `X` dummy atoms on both blocks** (X atoms persist until `builder.py:664`; they sit ~1.5 Å apart by construction and would dominate a false clash at every `phi`). Because local steric is often flat, `Clash` mainly **vetoes** clashing minima rather than selecting the answer.

The analytic seed `phi0` comes from `D(phi)` in closed form — either `atan2` of the projected transverse vectors (zero new scipy-feature dependency) or `align_vectors(weights=[inf, w])` (**verified working on scipy 1.15.3**, residual `~2e-16`), guarded against a near-axis-parallel secondary.

> **Mandatory pre-implementation experiment (gate):** on a built HKUST-1 and MOF-5, plot `E(phi)` and **prove it has a non-flat, single, correct (coplanar) minimum** before wiring any optimizer. If it is genuinely flat (isolated cylindrical linker), accept the twist is physically free and freeze at a deterministic convention. This directly answers the skeptic's strongest objection.

### 6.4 Optimizer (mirrors `locate()`)

1. Closed-form seed `phi0` from `D` (`atan2`/align-constrain), pinned to a **deterministic reference axis** (an explicit transverse seed vector), so the result does not depend on scipy's arbitrary in-plane choice.
2. Coarse 1-D grid `linspace(0, 2π, M)` (`M ≈ 24–36`) seeded at `phi0`, take argmin — the 1-D analogue of `locator.py:160-165`.
3. Local polish with `scipy.optimize.minimize_scalar(method='bounded')` on a bracket around the winner — the 1-D analogue of the builder's higher-accuracy re-locate.
4. Apply `R(u, phi*)`; keep `set_centroid` as today.

### 6.5 How it extends `Locator.locate`

It is a **strict 1-D extension** of `locate()`'s search→match→fit→keep-best onto the exactly-one DOF the 2-point degeneracy leaves open: the existing Kabsch fixes the axis (`locator.py:253-254`), the new code searches/refines `phi`. The node path, `locate()`, and `locate_with_permutation` are **untouched** (still used at `builder.py:394` for node relocation), so node placement, scaler, and CIF bond output are unchanged.

### 6.6 Files/functions to touch

1. **`src/pormake/edge_twist.py` (NEW)** — pure, dependency-light free functions (the heavy logic lives here, *not* inlined into `build()`, avoiding the fork's quality failure): `rotate_about_axis(positions, centroid, axis, phi)` (Rodrigues); `transverse_frame(bb, x_index)` (PCA-based, with degenerate fallback); `build_dihedral_objective(...)`; `build_clash_objective(edge_pos, neighbor_pos, cutoffs, excluded_indices)`; `seed_twist(axis, edge_sec, node_sec)` (`atan2` closed form).
2. **`src/pormake/locator.py`** — add `locate_edge_with_twist(self, target, bb, permutation, twist_objective=None, n_grid=30)`: run the existing axis-fixing fit, then seed + grid + `minimize_scalar`; apply `R(u, phi)` about `bb.centroid`; return `(bb, rmsd, phi)`. Scope a `warnings.catch_warnings` to **this method only** (do **not** touch the shared `find_best_orientation` at `locator.py:87`, or node placement changes).
3. **`src/pormake/builder.py:537-543`** — replace the single `locate_with_permutation` call with `locate_edge_with_twist`, passing a `twist_objective` **factory** built from `located_bbs[i1]/[i2]`, `a1`, `a2`, the edge X-neighbor indices, and the X-dummy indices. **Bind loop variables (`i1,i2,a1,a2`) as default args** to avoid Python late-binding bugs. Respect the existing `if edge_bb is None: continue` guard (`builder.py:513-515`); do not move the new code above it.
4. **`Builder.build(..., resolve_edge_twist=True)`** — opt-out flag so old behavior is recoverable for regression. **No** `build_by_type`/spglib coupling.
5. **`pyproject.toml`** — add an explicit `scipy>=1.11` floor (currently transitive only; verified `dependencies = [ase, jax, networkx, pymatgen]`), since `locator` calls scipy directly and the align-constrain path needs ≥1.11. The default `atan2` path needs no new feature.

### 6.7 How it provably addresses both constraints

- **C1 (post-relaxation):** every input is read inside the edge loop from post-scaler, post-node-placement world coordinates; the scaled topology has already replaced the ideal one (`builder.py:378-384`); nothing references `topology.spacegroup`/`edge_types`/spglib. Per-edge solves recover global symmetry where it survives and diverge where the Scaler broke it. Gate on `scaling_result` (available via `return_result`, `scaler.py:446`; `result.success` logged at `scaler.py:375`): if the relax failed, fall back to the deterministic seed and warn.
- **C2 (numerical):** `phi` is chosen by closed-form seed + 1-D grid + bounded local refine — the literal 1-D extension of `locate()`. No symmetry rule, no magic threshold.

## 7. Validation plan

### 7.1 Known structures (build with `resolve_edge_twist` True vs False)

- **HKUST-1 (tbo, Cu paddlewheel + BTC-type linker)** — assert: (a) linker plane/node-connector dihedral is consistent and near the coplanar optimum (**not** the arbitrary roll); (b) node positions + cell are **byte-identical** to the old build (only edge *internal* orientation changes — guaranteed by the X-on-axis fact); (c) min interatomic distance increases or stays above a clash threshold; (d) run-to-run determinism.
- **MOF-5 / IRMOF-1 (pcu, Zn4O + BDC = E1)** — same checks; pcu is high-symmetry so all symmetry-equivalent edges should converge to the same `phi` **emergently** (no orbit layer). **Use the real E1 (verified NOT C2, self-RMSD@180 = 0.60 Å)** to confirm the full `[0,2π)` search lands on the coplanar pose.

### 7.2 Asymmetric / chiral / degenerate linkers

- **Asymmetric ditopic linker on a low-symmetry net** — verify full `[0,2π)`, both perm branches evaluated, correct X-to-node mapping (bonds unchanged).
- **Chiral case** (`make_chiral_building_block`, `building_block.py:104`) — verify the proper-rotation twist suffices given fixed node placement (no improper branch added to the edge path).
- **Degenerate/cylindrical** — verify the transverse-radius guard fires only for truly cylindrical linkers (re-derive threshold from measured `transR`: E50=1.35, E8=2.46, E1=2.36) and that the build completes with a deterministic frozen `phi`.

### 7.3 Distorted net (the Constraint-1 stress test)

Pick a topology with a large Scaler max/min edge-length ratio (logged at `scaler.py:248-255`). Assert that ideal-net-equivalent edges take **different** twists where the relaxed environment differs, and that doing so **lowers** the objective vs forcing a shared twist — proving per-edge numerical solving rescues exactly the case a symmetry rule (geonho42) gets wrong.

### 7.4 Regression on existing tests

Run the existing suite (`tests/`); confirm node-path RMSDs, scaler output, and CIF bonds are unchanged with `resolve_edge_twist=False`. **Add the missing geometric/determinism assertions** — current integration tests check only atom **count/composition** (e.g. `test_build_with_edge_bb.py`), so a subtly wrong twist would pass today. Add an assert on run-to-run identical edge dihedral for MOF-5/HKUST-1, and re-baseline with the flag **on**.

### 7.5 Quantitative twist-quality metric

For every placed edge, report:
- **per-end dihedral residual** (deg) between linker transverse plane and node connector plane — primary correctness metric;
- **min framework interatomic distance** excluding intended bonds — clash metric;
- **twist consistency** = circular std of `phi` across ideal-equivalent edges (should be ~0 on undistorted nets, nonzero and *objective-justified* on distorted nets);
- **determinism** = max `|phi_runA − phi_runB|` over repeated builds (must be 0).

---

## 8. Open questions, risks, and first-prototype scope

### Open questions
1. **Is "coplanar" the universally correct target?** Some MOFs want a fixed **non-zero** dihedral. The dihedral objective should target a *configurable* offset (default 0), validated against known CIFs.
2. **Both-ends conflict on a rigid linker** (the genuine geometric impossibility when relaxation makes the two node planes non-coplanar): least-squares compromise + reported residual is proposed — confirm this is acceptable, and whether a tiny rigid node nudge is ever warranted.
3. **Non-local inter-linker clashes** (dense nets) are invisible to a per-edge local objective. Defer a global L-BFGS-B pass over all `phi` (MOFBuilder-style, reusing the Scaler's JAX stack) to a *later, optional* PR gated on a demonstrated clash the per-edge solve cannot resolve — **and if pursued, with no orbit spring.**
4. **Period detection**, if ever used to halve the domain, must be element-aware + Hungarian-matched with a documented, sensitivity-tested tolerance (E1=0.60, E26=1.19, E32=0.022 span the whole range — a single tol cannot separate them). Default recommendation: **don't halve; search `[0,2π)`.**

### Risks (and mitigations)
- **Flat objective in the canonical case** (skeptic's core objection) → mitigate by making **coplanarity primary** and **proving non-flatness on a built HKUST-1/MOF-5 before wiring the optimizer** (the §6.3 gate).
- **Fusion/X-dummy exclusion bug** → legitimate bonds register as clashes; mitigate with an explicit exclusion set (`a1,a2`, `connection_point_indices[perm]`, **all X atoms both blocks**) and a focused unit test.
- **Frame/centroid bug** (P2) → rotate world-space atoms about the world-space X-centroid after `set_centroid`, so the objective and neighbor atoms share one frame; unit-test that node neighbor distances are nonzero.
- **Closure late-binding** → bind `i1,i2,a1,a2` as default args per edge.
- **Unreliable Scaler minimum** → gate on `scaling_result.success`/`.fun` (`scaler.py:375,446`), fall back to seed + warn.
- **"geonho in disguise" perception** → no spglib, no ideal-net reads, no orbit spring; the PR must state explicitly that the twist is decided numerically on relaxed geometry.

### Concrete first-prototype scope (PR-1, minimal & mergeable)

Implement **the analytic per-edge core only**, behind `resolve_edge_twist`:

- `src/pormake/edge_twist.py` — `rotate_about_axis`, `transverse_frame` (PCA + degenerate fallback), `seed_twist` (`atan2`), `build_dihedral_objective`, `build_clash_objective` (with full X/fusion exclusion). (~120–180 lines, numpy-only.)
- `src/pormake/locator.py` — `locate_edge_with_twist` (seed → coarse grid → `minimize_scalar`), warnings scoped to this method. (~50–70 lines.)
- `src/pormake/builder.py:537-543` — swap the call; build the objective via a default-arg-bound factory. (~10 lines.)
- `pyproject.toml` — explicit `scipy>=1.11`.
- Tests — the §6.3 non-flatness gate experiment + the §7 HKUST-1/MOF-5 dihedral + determinism + node-unchanged regression.

This is a genuinely minimal, localized, idiomatic blast radius (one new module + one new Locator method + a one-call swap), far below the rejected fork's footprint, with the bond-invariant and align-constrain prerequisites **empirically verified in this repo**. The global joint relaxation and any period-halving are explicitly **out of PR-1 scope**.

- `align_vectors(weights=[inf, 1.0])` align-constrain: works, residual `~2.2e-16`.

- Transverse radius: E1 2.36, E8 2.46, E26 1.57, E32 4.99, **E50 1.35** Å (corrects the stale "E50/E8 are degenerate" claim).
- **E1 self-RMSD@180 = 0.6029 Å → NOT C2** (corrects the "period = π" assumption in two proposals).
- `pyproject.toml dependencies = [ase>=3.23.0, jax[cpu]>=0.4.13, networkx>=3.1, pymatgen>=2023.8.10]` — scipy transitive only; `natural_cutoffs` imported with `ase.utils`→`ase.neighborlist` fallback (`building_block.py:16-19`).
